records.name: Team Thompson Family Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia charity that works against hunger, low literacy, and poor access to hygiene supplies among low-income families. Its site names a holiday celebration and a summer basketball month.
records.what_you_do: The site asks visitors to donate, join its network, or get in touch through a contact form. It does not describe volunteer shifts or list dates for its events.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the group's site to ask how to join its network or help with its holiday or summer events.

records.notes: Filed as a family foundation, but the site describes a 501(c)(3) charity running public initiatives, so it is published rather than hidden as private. No dated events or news on the site; status rests only on a working site with no dates. Named initiatives are a holiday celebration and a summer hoops month, neither with dates. No email or phone published; contact form only. Verify before relying on it.

records.name: Thomas & Woods Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit for youth and families. It runs a summer basketball camp for kids, a yearly turkey drive, and a Martin Luther King Jr. speech contest that gives college scholarships.
records.what_you_do: Kids sign up for the summer basketball camp through the site's form. The group also runs a turkey drive for families each November and awards college scholarships through its speech contest.

schedule.text: A summer basketball camp (the site has a 2026 sign-up form) and an annual turkey drive held in November. The page gives no event dates for either.

first_step.how: Fill in the 2026 basketball camp sign-up form on the group's site.
first_step.basis: The camp sign-up form is public on the site, which is a clear way to join.

records.notes: Status 'active' rests on the camp sign-up form title, which gives 2026 with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out. Other dated items on the site are older: a 2021 speech contest, a summer 2023 newsletter, and a turkey drive dated only as November 19 with no year. The page does not say whether the group is a public charity or a private foundation; it runs public programs, so it is published. Contact is a form only; no email or phone published. Camp fees and camp dates are not stated.

first_step.how: Email the group at the address on its site to ask about volunteering at a painting event or applying to the free mural program.

records.notes: The events section says there are no events at the moment, and the site has no dated news. Status rests on a working site with no dates; the footer year is copyright, not evidence. records.name: Youth Capital Academy
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit started in 2025 that teaches kids and teens money skills, business building, and leadership. It has worked with high schools and held a youth business fair.
records.what_you_do: Young people learn money skills, entrepreneurship and leadership, with mentoring; the group reports helping more than 15 young people start businesses in 2025. Families and students can use the contact form on the site to get involved or ask about enrollment.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the group's site, or email info@youthcapitalacademy.org, to ask how to enroll.

records.notes: The Programs and Enrollment pages returned 404, so ages, schedule, cost, location and enrollment rules are unknown; re-check the live site before relying on this record. The newest dated item is 'Our Impact in 2025' with no month, so status is probably_active and last_sign_of_life is left out. The 2026 footer year is copyright, not evidence. The site says the group was founded in 2025.

records.name: African American Genealogy Group
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps people trace African American family history. It holds free public meetings with a speaker most months, and members can also join workshops and state group meetings.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free general meeting on the second Tuesday of the month, except July and August. There is a social hour at 6 pm, and the talk starts at 6:30 pm. Registration is on the group's site.

schedule.text: General meetings on the second Tuesday of the month, except July and August. Social hour at 6 pm, talk at 6:30 pm.

cost.text: Free and open to the public

first_step.how: Register for the next general meeting through the registration page on aagg.org, then arrive for the 6 pm social hour.
first_step.basis: General meetings are free and open to the public, and registration is the stated way in. The next talk is aimed at beginners.

records.notes: The next meeting is listed for Tuesday, October 13, 2026, a talk for beginners; that listing is the status evidence. The text read from the site gives no venue for the in-person meeting, so check the registration page before this goes live. The mailing address is P.O. Box 27356, Philadelphia, PA 19118, which is not a meeting place. Membership dues are not published. The site uses a contact form only. A 2024 CBS Philadelphia article (updated February 29, 2024) is where the website name came from.

records.name: Beacon Theatre Productions
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit theater company that stages affordable plays to reach new audiences. It holds open auditions for a short play festival made of staged readings.
records.what_you_do: Non-union actors can audition for the short play festival, which pays a $50 stipend. Rehearsals and performances are in Philadelphia, including at a church in Germantown. The site does not list classes or volunteer jobs.

schedule.text: Auditions, rehearsals and performances for the short play festival. The site gives weekdays and dates with no year, so confirm the year before planning around them.

first_step.how: Email the group at the address on its site to ask about the next short play festival audition and to have the audition pages sent to you.

records.notes: Dates are written as weekday plus day with no year. The footer says 2021, which is copyright only, but it suggests the page was last updated around then. The weekdays fit more than one year (for example 2020 and 2026), so no year was assigned and status is unknown. Confirm current festival dates with the group. The mailing address is a PO Box (PO Box 4026, Philadelphia, PA 19118), not a venue. Show venues: a church in Germantown (no street address given) and a Northwest Philadelphia location still to be announced.

notes: Budget: WebSearch 2 of 2 used (Tri-State Basketball, African American Genealogy Group). Fetch: 23 calls, 17 pages read. Verdicts: 6 publish, 8 hide (private), 1 not_a_group. Decision for the owner: seven IRS-only groups had no readable website and no program information (Royalty Supreme All Stars, Teens N Technology, Trapdoor, Tri-State Basketball, Tzedakah House, Women's Solo Project, Wearebetter). The eighth hidden group, African Diaspora Renaissance Corporation, has a Coming Soon page and no programs. The tier 1 default is an unknown publish record for groups nothing was found about. I hid these instead, because publish means joinable and a visitor would have nothing to act on. If you want them listed as unknown, flip the verdict to publish and add a summary. Several batch website fields held a name, not a web address (Royalty, Teens N Technology, Tzedakah House, Tri-State, Women's Solo Project, Agro-Export). Name collision: Philadelphia Youth Basketball Inc (EIN 47-3758442) is not Tri-State Basketball Inc (EIN 851058390). Team Thompson is filed as a family foundation but describes itself as a 501(c)(3) running public initiatives, so it is published at low confidence. Thomas & Woods does not say whether it is a public charity or a private foundation; it runs public programs, so it is published. Groups with a readable website but no dated evidence are probably_active or unknown, never active.
